text:
sam: Quick sync — customers pushing for streaming semantics decision. Two high-priority asks: mobile-first customer wants SSE (no websockets via their proxy), platform partner wants websocket multiplexing for many concurrent chats. Need recommended MVP surface + launch gates. :thinking:

maria: thanks. can we scope an MVP that satisfies both commercially? maybe SSE default + websocket as opt-in later. outline: protocol handshake, delta payload schema, finish reasons, resume/fallback doc.

aj: from infra POV SSE is way easier to route through existing LB+nginx. websockets need sticky sessions or LB changes. SSE also plays nicer with HTTP/2+gRPC proxies on mobile.

leo: scoring tradeoffs: SSE pros = simple (proxies, retries), cons = no bidirectional multiplexing; WS pros = multiplexing, lower per-connection cost for many chats, cons = ops complexity + harder autoscaling.

nina: product-level ask: customers expect consistent finish semantics across transports. we should enumerate finish reasons and ensure SDK returns identical final objects, regardless of SSE/WS.

ops-bot: deployment note: canary on Dedicated first, then Hosted. telemetry flagging required for protocol choice. :white_check_mark:

sam: propose MVP decisions: 1) support SSE first (mobile customer unblock). 2) define delta schema v0 that is transport-agnostic (small JSON fragments). 3) explicit finish_reason enum: ["stop", "error", "cancelled", "max_tokens", "tool_call", "internal_fail"]. 4) SDK shim maps transport events to same callbacks.

maria: agree with transport-agnostic deltas. suggest delta shape example:
``` 
{ "type": "delta", "chunk_id": "c1", "role": "assistant", "delta": "text fragment", "meta": {"tokens": 12} }
{ "type": "finish", "reason": "stop", "meta": {"deterministic_id": "abc123"} }
```
This keeps parsing simple and allows structured output deltas later.

aj: need server work items: SSE endpoint stream backends, delta batching config, kv-cache propagation for resume, metrics hooks for open connections. estimate: 2 sprint infra + 1 sprint runtime.

leo: client SDK work: streaming shim for JS/py/go that exposes identical on_delta/on_finish callbacks and auto-falls back to poll-based chunking if transport unsupported. docs + migration guide needed. estimate: 2 engineers x 3 weeks.

nina: launch gating checklist (suggested):
- protocol conformance tests (SSE + WS handshake)
- SDK parity tests across transports
- perf SLOs (p50/p90 latency targets for 1k concurrent mobile clients)
- resume/fallback tested with flaky proxies
- finish_reason canonicalization validated on real prompts
- API breaking changes documented + deprecation window
- customer sign-off from two pilot accounts

sam: prioritization note: if resource-constrained, cut websocket multiplexing from MVP and schedule for Q2 milestone. must still design handshake so WS can be added without changing client-facing schema.

maria: one more nuance: structured output/function calls — we should stream both raw delta text and a separate structured delta when available. signature:
```
{ "type":"structured", "name":"function_call", "payload": {"name":"calc","args":"{...}"} }
```
SDK should buffer structured deltas and emit as they arrive.

aj: ops question — how do we handle finish_reason for partial cancels (user interrupts) vs model internal stops? propose distinct reasons: "user_cancel" and "internal_stop" to help billing/metrics.

sam: good call. update finish_reason list to include "user_cancel" and keep "internal_fail". also tie billing delta to "tokens_consumed" in finish meta.

leo: I'll prototype the JS SDK shim next week and post a short RFC with example callbacks + migration notes.

nina: i'll draft launch checklist + QA plan and tag the two pilot customers. schedule a review with infra + eng-runtime early next week.

sam: decision captured: SSE-first MVP, transport-agnostic delta schema v0, expanded finish_reason list, WS postponed unless bandwidth allows. owners: maria (schema + runtime), aj (infra), leo (SDK), nina (QA + launches). next: owners to post concrete RFCs in #product by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
